name: Ảnh hiện dần
notes: chapters = seconds in film.mp4 where the film waits for a tap, taken from scene.html by stops.py (it runs the scene's own rests code): the title frame, one stop in each of the six polaroids (PAUSE.inBeat into its beat: the print has developed, its caption is written and its note is up), the climax (PAUSE.climax: the last polaroid lies blank, waiting to be tapped), and the last frame (the table, the pile, the veil). Each sits a quarter of a frame into its frame, so a seek shows that frame and round(t * fps) finds its boxes. The film is 480 frames (20 s): the scene plays 30 s straight through, and fewer frames make the polaroids jump. hints = the scene's own words at those stops (WORDS.cue, ui.next, WORDS.hint, ui.skip); a card can override them with "chapters". reveal = null: no 3D envelope; after the last stop a tap opens the letter. slots.json: cap0 ... cap5 are the captions handwritten on the six polaroids' strips and last is the caption on the last polaroid (label, Patrick Hand); line0 ... line5 are the notes on the paper slips (caption, Vollkorn italic). slots.json photos (7 places): the buyer's photos go onto the polaroids' pictures in the order the film shows them, coffee, rain, lanterns, pass, beach, pho (the six story prints) and us (the last polaroid); a polaroid without a photo keeps the drawing the scene uses. Each place is the picture itself (aspect 1.003: the 288 x 287 px the scene paints; not the white frame or the strip), measured frame by frame in render.html stepped as render.py steps it and checked against the film's pixels: its four corners, and a clip where a later print, the last polaroid or a slip (once it is at least half opaque) lies over it, so the pile builds up over the photos as it did over the drawings. A place starts when its print's chemistry starts to lift (before that the blank print hides its drawing); develop is the chemistry alone (1 - the .chem layer's opacity), from the blank (#2b312e, the chemistry's own colour) to the photo. The film's light is laid over the photo as overlays, in the film's order: on the place, the prints' gloss (the .gloss gradient, exact); per frame, while a print develops, its vignette (.edge, as two gradients across and down) and its tint and filter (one colour, as opaque as the filter takes from the contrast, the colour that comes closest over the whole colour cube); the shadow of the last polaroid landing over pho (frames 363 to 372, one gradient each, fitted to the film); the afternoon light (.hour is soft-light, which the painter cannot blend: the plain colour that comes closest; over the last polaroid its own .hour, a gradient across it); the scrim over the top of the film (exact); and the veil at the end (along its radius, exact to a gradient). The last polaroid's place starts after the tap and follows it as it turns over (four corners in perspective, the photo squeezed by its aspect; at frame 451, nearly edge-on, a flat parallelogram clipped to it, as the painter's pieces still leave seams on so thin a place). A place lying straight on whole pixels is exact; a turned or moving one is grown by a pixel to cover its soft edge. Left out: the contact shadows of prints lying on a picture (an L along the covering card's edges, under 2 levels on average, that no single gradient follows), the soft-light's exact curve and the tint's colour blend (approximated as above). Compromises: the player paints words straight, so in the film the polaroid lying in the middle, the strip's handwriting and the slips are not tilted, and a caption shows only while its polaroid lies in the middle: it fades in while the marker would write it (no left-to-right writing) and fades out before the print slides into the pile, so the prints in the pile have blank strips; the last caption shows after the last print develops and fades as it turns over. Every slip is four lines tall, the note centred in it. fonts = the faces the player paints these slots in (latin, latin-ext and vietnamese).
